BUS.G12.T3.SECURITIES.A1.title: Investment: securities
BUS.G12.T3.SECURITIES.A1.description: A range of business investment opportunities: business investments and the JSE, types of shares, unit trusts and government retail bonds; returns such as dividends and interest; and calculations including the difference between simple and compound interest.
BUS.G12.T3.SECURITIES.A1.recovery_strategy: Simple interest is on the original amount only; compound interest is on the amount plus past interest, so it grows faster. Shares pay dividends (a share of profit); savings and bonds pay interest. Unit trusts spread money across many investments.

questions.question: The JSE is the Johannesburg _________ Exchange, where shares are bought and sold.
questions.memo: The JSE (Johannesburg Stock Exchange) is the market where shares in listed companies are traded.

questions.question: What does owning a share in a company give you?
questions.memo: A share represents part-ownership of a company, entitling the holder to a share of profits (dividends).

questions.question: True or false: Shares can pay their owners dividends.
questions.memo: Companies may pay dividends — a share of their profit — to shareholders.

questions.question: _________ interest is calculated only on the original amount invested.
questions.memo: Simple interest is worked out only on the original principal, the same amount each period.

questions.question: Compound interest is calculated on:
options: The original amount plus the interest already earned
questions.expected: The original amount plus the interest already earned
questions.memo: Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest, so it grows faster than simple interest.

questions.question: True or false: A government retail bond is a form of investment.
questions.memo: A government retail bond is a relatively safe investment in which you lend money to the government and earn interest.

questions.question: Sort each item into the type of investment it describes.

items.text: Part-ownership of a single listed company
A pooled fund spread across many investments
Lending money to the government for interest
Earns dividends when the company profits
Managed by a fund manager on investors' behalf

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Shares = part-ownership earning dividends; unit trusts = pooled, managed funds; government retail bonds = lending to the state for interest.

questions.question: What is the difference between dividends and interest?
options: Dividends are a share of a company's profit; interest is a reward for lending or saving money
Dividends are paid on savings; interest is paid on shares
Neither is a form of return
questions.expected: Dividends are a share of a company's profit; interest is a reward for lending or saving money
questions.memo: Shares earn dividends (a portion of profit); savings and bonds earn interest (a reward for lending money).

questions.question: What is the simple interest on R5 000 invested at 10% per year for 2 years?
questions.memo: Simple interest = R5 000 × 10% × 2 = R500 × 2 = R1 000.

questions.question: A _________ trust pools many investors' money to buy a spread of shares and other assets.
questions.memo: A unit trust pools investors' money, which a fund manager spreads across many investments to reduce risk.

questions.question: Why does compound interest grow an investment faster than simple interest?
options: Because the interest itself earns further interest over time
Because it ignores the original amount
Because it is calculated only once
Because it removes interest each year
questions.expected: Because the interest itself earns further interest over time
questions.memo: With compounding, each period's interest is added to the balance and then earns interest too, so growth accelerates.

questions.question: True or false: Investing in shares carries the risk that their value can fall.
questions.memo: Share prices rise and fall, so there is a real risk that an investment in shares can lose value.

questions.question: Sort each return into whether it comes from shares or from lending/saving.

items.text: A dividend paid out of company profit
A rise in a share's market value
Interest from a fixed savings account
A share of profits distributed to owners
Interest earned on a retail bond

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Dividends and share-value growth come from shares; interest comes from lending or saving money (bonds, savings accounts).

questions.question: What is the simple interest on R2 000 invested at 8% per year for 3 years?
questions.memo: Simple interest = R2 000 × 8% × 3 = R160 × 3 = R480.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of a unit trust for a small investor?
options: It spreads money across many investments, reducing risk
It guarantees the investor will never lose money
It gives full control of a single company
It avoids all fees and charges
questions.expected: It spreads money across many investments, reducing risk
questions.memo: A unit trust diversifies across many assets, so a small investor is less exposed to any single investment failing.

questions.question: A _________ is a portion of a company that an investor can buy on the stock exchange.
questions.memo: A share is a unit of ownership in a company that can be bought and sold, for example on the JSE.

questions.question: R1 000 is invested for 2 years at 10% per year. Which earns more — simple or compound interest — and roughly by how much?
questions.memo: Simple = R1 000 × 10% × 2 = R200. Compound = R1 000 × 1.1² − R1 000 = R1 210 − R1 000 = R210. Compound earns R10 more.

questions.question: An investor wants low risk and a predictable return. Which option fits best?
options: Shares in a single small start-up
Borrowing to bet on one volatile share
Putting everything into one speculative company
questions.memo: A government retail bond is relatively low-risk with predictable interest, suiting a cautious investor; single shares carry more risk.

questions.question: Why do many investors spread their money across different types of investments?
options: Diversifying reduces the impact if any single investment performs badly
It guarantees the highest possible return
questions.expected: Diversifying reduces the impact if any single investment performs badly
questions.memo: Spreading investments (diversification) means a loss in one is cushioned by others, lowering overall risk.

questions.question: A young investor saving for retirement in 30 years asks why compound interest matters so much over a long period.
options: Over many years, interest earning interest causes the investment to grow dramatically
Compound interest only matters for one year
Time makes no difference to compound growth
Compound interest shrinks an investment over time
questions.expected: Over many years, interest earning interest causes the investment to grow dramatically
questions.memo: Compounding builds on itself, so over decades the growth becomes very large — time is a powerful ally for long-term investors.
